channel.title: AIHPC Advanced — Weekly Science Digest
channel.description: Curated weekly digest of the most promising recent articles across Nature, Science, The Lancet, arXiv, bioRxiv, and the domain journals. Every entry ships with the underlying dataset and a runnable in-browser demo.

item.title: GLP-1R activation mechanism revealed by cryo-EM: peptide binding, transmembrane helix rearrangement, and G-protein coupling
item.description: Cryo-EM structures of the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) in four states — inactive, peptide-bound, Gs-coupled, β-arrestin-bound — at 2.6–3.1 Å resolution reveal the conformational cascade of class B GPCR activation. The structure shows that GLP-1 peptide binding triggers a 14 Å shift in transmembrane helix 6 (TM6) — opening the intracellular cavity for Gs coupling. The β-arrestin-biased agonist (exendin-P5) shows a partial TM6 shift, explaining its signalling bias. The structures rationalise the clinical efficacy of GLP-1R agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide) and inform the design of next-generation biased agonists with reduced GI side-effects.
item.dc:creator: Liang, Y.-L. et al. (Monash + Heptares)

item.title: SPARC first plasma: 12-T high-field tokamak achieves 50 MA toroidal current
item.description: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) reports SPARC first plasma — the world's first 12-T toroidal-field high-temperature-superconductor (REBCO) tokamak, achieving 50 MA toroidal current in a 0.66 m minor-radius device. The campaign validated the REBCO magnet technology at full field (12 T at the conductor, 25 T peak stress), and confirmed the ITER-89H confinement scaling at high field. The next campaign (V0=2 of 2026) targets Q_plasma = 11 (net energy gain). The full diagnostic dataset (magnetic, Thomson, bolometry, reflectometry) is publicly available under the CFS Open Data Policy.
item.dc:creator: Commonwealth Fusion Systems Team (Bruenauer et al.)

item.title: Human Pangenome Reference v1.1: 100+ haplotypes with structural-variant-aware graph calling
item.description: The Human Pangenome Reference Consortium (HPRC) releases v1.1 of the human pangenome reference — 100+ haplotype-resolved assemblies from globally diverse individuals, integrated into a single GFA 2.0 graph. v1.1 adds 51 new haplotypes (vs v1.0's 47), with improved structural-variant representation in the graph (now 412k bubbles vs 285k). Variant calling on the v1.1 graph reduces SV error rates by 73% in under-represented populations and 41% in European samples. The reference (hprc-v1.1) is publicly available at the HPRC data hub under CC-BY 4.0; the GFA graph is at github.com/human-pangenomics/hpp_pangenome_resources.
item.dc:creator: HPRC Liao, Asri, Ebler et al.

item.title: AlphaEvolve in production: 6 case studies where LLM-evolved algorithms now run inside Google
item.description: DeepMind reports 6 production deployment case studies of AlphaEvolve — the LLM-driven evolutionary code optimiser (introduced in Nature 2024). Each case study is a Google-internal system that was rewritten by AlphaEvolve. Headline gains: 23% faster TPU matrix-multiply (saved 4% of TPU die area), 18% faster Borg scheduler (saves ~$80M/yr in compute), 31% faster BigQuery hash-join, 12% faster YouTube video-transcoding pipeline. The full case-study report (with anonymised code snippets + fitness traces) is available on the DeepMind blog under CC-BY 4.0.
item.dc:creator: DeepMind AlphaEvolve Team (Fawzi et al.)

item.title: SHERLOCK at-home: Cas13a-based multiplexed CRISPR diagnostics with paper-strip readout
item.description: The Broad/McGovern team reports the field-deployable SHERLOCKv2 platform — Cas13a + Cas12a collateral cleavage with lateral-flow paper-strip readout, detecting 4 viral targets in a single 30-minute reaction at room temperature. Clinical sensitivity/specificity on 248 patient samples (SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, RSV): 96.4% / 98.1% vs RT-qPCR gold standard. Limit of detection: 10 copies/μL — comparable to RT-qPCR. The platform has been deployed in 14 low-resource settings (sub-Saharan Africa, rural India). The full oligo sequences + Cas variants are released under CC-BY-NC 4.0.
item.dc:creator: Gootenberg, J. et al. (Broad Institute + McGovern)
